inputFigure.alt: The fresh shipment workflow shows Next review step, the responsible shipment-lead role, and Review answer: Shipment identity and units. Other required review steps remain collapsed.
inputFigure.caption: The next review task is explicit. Selecting it opens the required answer; it does not accept the answer, evaluate an assessment or authorize an operating action.

steps.title: Start with the shipment commitment.
paragraphs: The workflow opens at Next action. For a fresh case, Next review step identifies the next required answer or assessment and its responsible role. Follow that action to the relevant question, inspect the supplied information and explicitly accept it only after review.

The commitment is still ORD-104: 100 cases for DC-X, reserved by noon on November 17 and received by 5 p.m. on November 20, with 30 minutes allowed to respond to verification. In the completed brief, expand Supporting findings → Delivery commitment to inspect these recorded details. Commitment, Arrangements and Prerequisites & records remain available when reviewing the inputs.
steps.alt: The app’s Delivery commitment section records DC-X, a November 17 noon reservation cutoff, November 20 at 5 p.m. receipt, 30 response minutes and 100 cases.
steps.caption: The delivery commitment is available on request beneath the decision brief. Its dates, quantity and response allowance are unchanged.

steps.title: See what the records establish.
paragraphs: Follow the next review task to evaluate Review the transportation records. Inspect its decision screen before choosing Accept result for this review: the business question, supported answer or remaining uncertainty appears first.

The supplied portal capture lists SP-A, but does not settle transportation registration for this exact shipment. Open Why this finding? for contrasting possible explanations; registered and not_registered both remain possible. Keep both in planning. Technical inspection opens the complete evidence assessment if needed.
steps.alt: The current evidence decision screen displays the registration question, remaining uncertainty and business explanation, with Why this finding? available for supporting explanations.
steps.caption: The business answer and its uncertainty lead. Possible explanations are available on request and do not supply probability weights.

steps.title: Compare more than the freight quote.
paragraphs: Evaluate Compare complete shipment arrangements and inspect the decision screen. Available options compares the complete arrangements, with dollar costs, the configured priority and failed conditions. The same preparation, timing, resource, permission and cash checks still apply across both retained transportation states.

The $6,000 backup passes every mandatory obligation in both states. The $4,000 direct plan is blocked in the not-registered state, so its lower price does not make it an available choice on the current evidence. Accept the planning result after reviewing that comparison.
steps.alt: The compact shipment decision prefers Backup at $6,000 and shows Direct at $4,000 blocked by Complete accepted order.
steps.caption: The default screen presents the supported choice and its blocker in business terms. The complete calculation remains available behind the decision.

steps.title: Open the requirement behind the blocker.
paragraphs: Select Direct in Available options and expand Selected option details. The complete assignment, mandatory requirement results and Conditions needing attention show where its support fails. Open the relevant detail view or Technical inspection for the full plan-by-situation report.

Complete accepted order fails because the direct ship point must be transportation-registered for the exact shipment scope. The preparation, permission, timing, receiving-window, expense, and cash obligations pass in this situation. That tells the team which question needs resolving before the cheaper shipment plan could be supported.
steps.alt: Selected option details for Direct retain its assignment, mandatory requirement results and failed registration condition in the not_registered situation.
steps.caption: Selected details expose the failed condition without replacing the compact decision with the entire report by default.

steps.title: Ask whether another check is worth buying.
paragraphs: Evaluate and review Check complete responses after fast verification and Check complete responses after slow verification. These assessments test the complete shipment choices still available after each possible report. Then select finance reviewer to evaluate and review Compare verification with reserving now.

Under the example’s explicitly hypothetical 50/50 probability assessment and stipulated perfectly accurate verification, the $200 fast verification supports an expected total cost of $5,200, including its fee. That is $800 below reserving the backup immediately. If registration is confirmed, the response can select direct shipment; if nonregistration is confirmed, it selects backup.

Inspect the learning decision screen: it puts acting now, expected improvement, the preferred investigation and unavailable options together. The monetary comparison is formatted in dollars. Responses to possible results retains the report-dependent actions and operating eligibility on request.
steps.alt: The learning decision compares acting now at minus $6,000 with fast verification at minus $5,200, shows $800 expected improvement and leaves slow verification unavailable.
steps.caption: The decision-first learning view shows expected payoff after costs in dollars. The same finding is expressed as $5,200 expected cost and $800 expected improvement in the brief.

steps.title: A cheaper answer can arrive too late.
paragraphs: The decision screen identifies when the selected investigation can support a response. For the full timing chart, open Technical inspection → Inspect complete report, select Verification before reservation and switch Review timing to Timeline. The fast report arrives at 10 a.m.; with the 30-minute allowance, the response is ready at 10:30 a.m., before the noon cutoff.

The $50 slow report arrives at 2 p.m. Its response would be ready at 2:30 p.m., after reservation closes. It cannot support a timely choice, even though its fee is lower. Compare when a result can change the action, as well as what the result might say.
steps.alt: The live app’s review-timing timeline shows the fast response ready at minute 630 and the slow response ready at minute 870, after the reservation deadline.
steps.caption: The complete timing analysis remains available by explicit inspection. Its original minute values are unchanged: 630 is 10:30 a.m., 720 noon and 870 2:30 p.m.

steps.title: Keep the recommendation and its conditions together.
paragraphs: Return to decision brief after accepting the current assessment results. Next action leads with the supported $6,000 shipment proposal and the fast-verification proposal with $5,200 expected cost and $800 expected improvement. Proposal details and Supporting findings keep the complete basis available on request.

Expand Authority and next operating actions to inspect the recorded $250 verification purchase limit and separate release authority. These business proposals differ from Next review step, which identifies the next required answer or result review while the case is incomplete. Opening that task does not accept it or carry out a purchase, booking or release.

Use Review files & history → Export workflow run for the portable review, or Download decision brief for its recorded basis. If a quote, record or approval changes, review and accept the updated answer, then reassess the affected findings. A previous calculation remains historical support, not an assessment of the changed inputs.
